description: We are a trio of passionate technology and Space exploration enthusiasts brought together by the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Combining our skills in web development, UI/UX Design, and storytelling, we are tackling the "Abondoned but not forgotten" challenge, our mission is to build an interactive experience that connects the public with the science and legacy of these technological pioneers.
summary: ORBITAL Space Challenge is a zero-cost, lightweight web portal designed to tell the story of the human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Addressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, the platform transforms scattered technical archives and complex aerospace papers into an accessible, visual experience for school-age space enthusiasts, students, and educators. Structured around three core questions—What was left behind? (Discarded Equipment), How did it work? (Technologies Used), and Who built and used it? (Scientists Behind Those Objects). The portal catalogs iconic artifacts such as Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, the Apollo Guidance Computer, SNAP-27 RTGs, and Mars rovers like Spirit, Opportunity, and InSight. Additionally, ORBITAL integrates an interactive AI assistant powered by Groq (Llama 3) on Streamlit, allowing visitors to ask real-time questions about space history and hardware engineering. Built with native HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript without heavy frameworks, ORBITAL loads rapidly on low-end devices and school computers, democratizing access to NASA’s extraterrestrial exploration heritage.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

ORBITAL Space Challenge is an educational web platform that indexes and explains the engineering behind discarded space hardware on the Moon (~180 tonnes of Apollo and robotic artifacts) and Mars (landers and rovers). Users navigate through three thematic pillars:

1. Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars: Historical records of Apollo LM descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Surveyor probes, Viking 1 & 2, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity and much more.

2. Technologies Used in Equipments: Plain-language breakdowns of aluminized Kapton/Mylar insulation, hand-woven Apollo Guidance Computer (AGC) core rope memory, Aerozine 50 hypergolic propulsion, Vectran landing airbags, SNAP-27 plutonium-238 RTGs, and radiation-hardened RAD6000 processors, for example.

3. Scientists Behind Those Objects: Profiles of pioneers including Margaret Hamilton, Eugene Shoemaker, Alan Binder, and Steve Squyres.

To enhance interactivity, a floating "Ask AI" button connects users to a custom Streamlit web app powered by the Groq API (Llama 3), parameterized with the project's historical knowledge base to answer student questions in real time without storing personal data.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE:

- Frontend: Semantic HTML5, modular CSS3 (glassmorphism UI, responsive flexbox/grid layouts, smooth CSS transitions), and Vanilla JavaScript (zero third-party JS frameworks).

- Interactive AI Module: Python, Streamlit Community Cloud, and Groq API (Llama 3).

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and Vercel Edge Network.

IMPACT, ACCESSIBILITY, ENERGY & COST:

Designed specifically for students and teachers, ORBITAL prioritizes digital inclusion and sustainability. By avoiding heavy frameworks, total page weights stay under 210 KB with sub-0.3s DOM load times and 98–100/100 Google Lighthouse performance and accessibility scores. This reduces bandwidth and energy consumption while ensuring smooth performance on mobile phones and older school computers at a total infrastructure cost of USD 0.00.
